CYBER INCIDENT RESPONSE

Standard Operating Procedure

| Document Title | Cyber Incident Response Standard Operating Procedure |
| --- | --- |
| Document ID | SOP-CSIRT-001 |
| Version | 1.2 |
| Prepared By | IT Security Team |
| Reviewed By | CISO |
| Date | March 2024 |
| Status | Active |

# 1. Purpose

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the process for detecting, responding to, and recovering from cybersecurity incidents at the bank. The goal is to minimise the impact of security incidents on the bank's operations, customers, and reputation.

This document should be used by the IT Security team and other relevant stakeholders when a cybersecurity incident is suspected or confirmed.

# 2. Scope

This SOP applies to all cybersecurity incidents affecting the bank's information systems, networks, applications, and data. This includes:

All IT systems and infrastructure owned or operated by the bank

Third-party systems that process or store bank data

All employees, contractors, and vendors who have access to bank systems

The following are out of scope for this procedure:

Physical security incidents (refer to the Physical Security policy)

Fraud incidents not involving a cybersecurity component

# 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Cybersecurity Incident | An event that has or may have an adverse effect on the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information systems or data. |
| Threat Actor | An individual, group, or organisation responsible for carrying out a cyberattack. |
| Indicator of Compromise (IoC) | Evidence that a system or network has been compromised, such as unusual network traffic or unexpected file changes. |
| SIEM | Security Information and Event Management system used to aggregate and correlate security logs. |
| RTO | Recovery Time Objective â?? the target duration for restoring operations after an incident. |

# 4. Roles and Responsibilities

The following roles are involved in the incident response process. Each team should be aware of their responsibilities and be ready to act when an incident occurs.

| Role | Responsibilities |
| --- | --- |
| CISO | Overall accountability for cybersecurity. Should be informed of significant incidents. |
| IT Security Team / SOC | Monitors security alerts, conducts triage, coordinates response activities. |
| Incident Response Manager | Manages the response process and communication during an incident. Usually the IT Security Head. |
| IT Operations | Supports containment and recovery activities as directed by the security team. |
| Legal / Compliance | Advises on regulatory and legal obligations. Involved when required. |
| Senior Management | Should be kept informed of major incidents that affect the business. |
| HR Department | Involved in cases where an employee is suspected of wrongdoing. |

# 5. Incident Classification

Not all security events are incidents. When an alert is received, the SOC analyst should assess whether it represents a genuine incident or a false positive.

Incidents should be classified based on their potential impact to the organisation. Higher impact incidents should be escalated to senior management and the CISO as appropriate.

Factors to consider when assessing impact include:

Number of systems or users affected

Sensitivity of data involved

Whether services have been disrupted

Likelihood of financial loss or reputational damage

# 6. Incident Response Process

The incident response process follows six phases as outlined below. Teams should move through each phase systematically.

| Step | Phase | Key Actions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Detection & Identification | Security alerts received via SIEM, EDR, or user reports. SOC analyst reviews and performs initial triage. |
| 2 | Initial Assessment | Assess the nature and scope of the incident. Determine if it is a genuine security incident or a false positive. |
| 3 | Containment | Take steps to contain the incident and prevent further damage. Actions will depend on the type of incident. |
| 4 | Eradication | Remove the threat from the environment. This may include removing malware, disabling compromised accounts, and patching vulnerabilities. |
| 5 | Recovery | Restore affected systems and services to normal operations. Verify that systems are clean before bringing them back online. |
| 6 | Communication | Notify relevant stakeholders as appropriate. This includes management, affected users, and potentially external parties. |

## 6.1 Detection and Identification

Security incidents may be detected through various sources including:

SIEM alerts and correlation rules

Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) alerts

Reports from employees or customers

Threat intelligence feeds

External notifications (e.g., from vendors or law enforcement)

When an alert is received, the SOC analyst should review the available information and determine whether it represents a genuine security incident.

## 6.2 Containment

Once an incident is confirmed, the priority is to contain the threat and prevent it from spreading. Containment actions may include:

Isolating affected systems from the network

Disabling compromised user accounts

Blocking malicious IP addresses or domains at the firewall or proxy

Suspending affected services if necessary

The Incident Response Manager should decide which containment actions are appropriate based on the specific circumstances of the incident.

## 6.3 Eradication

After the incident has been contained, the source of the compromise should be identified and removed. This may include:

Removing malware from affected systems using antivirus or EDR tools

Revoking and resetting compromised credentials

Applying security patches to address the vulnerability exploited

Reviewing and strengthening access controls

## 6.4 Recovery

Systems should be restored to normal operation only after the threat has been fully eradicated. Before bringing systems back online, the team should verify that:

All malware or malicious artefacts have been removed

Patching has been applied where relevant

Access controls have been reviewed and tightened

Systems should be monitored closely for a period following recovery to detect any signs of re-compromise.

# 7. Communication and Escalation

Communication during an incident is important. The Incident Response Manager is responsible for keeping relevant stakeholders informed.

## 7.1 Internal Communication

The following stakeholders should be notified as appropriate during an incident:

CISO â?? should be informed of significant incidents promptly

Senior management â?? to be notified if the incident has a material business impact

Affected business units â?? to be kept informed of progress and recovery timelines

HR â?? if an employee is involved

## 7.2 External Communication

External communication should be managed carefully and approved by senior management before release.

Customer notifications â?? if customer data has been compromised, customers may need to be informed

Media inquiries â?? all media inquiries should be directed to the Communications team

Law enforcement â?? the Legal team will advise if law enforcement involvement is required

# 8. Documentation and Evidence

All incidents should be documented in the incident tracking system. The following information should be recorded:

Date and time the incident was detected

Nature of the incident

Systems and data affected

Actions taken during response

Outcome and resolution

Documentation should be completed as soon as practicable after the incident is resolved.

# 9. Training and Awareness

All IT security staff should be familiar with this SOP. Annual security awareness training is conducted for all employees.

Tabletop exercises and simulations may be conducted periodically to test the bank's incident response readiness.

# 10. Document Review

This SOP should be reviewed and updated periodically, or following a significant security incident. The IT Security team is responsible for maintaining this document.

# Appendix A â?? Contact List

In the event of an incident, the following contacts should be notified as appropriate. This list should be maintained and kept up to date by the IT Security team.

| Role | Name | Contact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CISO | [Name] | [Phone / Email] |
| IT Security Head | [Name] | [Phone / Email] |
| Head of IT Operations | [Name] | [Phone / Email] |
| Chief Compliance Officer | [Name] | [Phone / Email] |
| Legal Counsel | [Name] | [Phone / Email] |
